extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for measuring and reporting the performance of press releases, including distribution, engagement, pickup (earned media), and business outcomes, plus quality requirements for releases to be measurable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total impressions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A distribution metric indicating how many times the release was potentially seen; listed under Distribution Metrics as a top-of-funnel measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic reach
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures the geographic spread of where the release was viewed or picked up (regions, countries, cities); useful for understanding market penetration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry vertical coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks which industry sectors saw or republished the release to assess relevance across verticals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device type (mobile vs desktop)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segmentation of impressions/engagement by device to optimize format and timing for audience device preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click-through rate to landing page
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An engagement metric measuring percent of viewers who click from the release to the landing page; ties distribution to direct site activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time on page
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures how long visitors spend on the landing page reached via the release — indicates depth of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scroll depth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks how far readers scroll on the landing page (proxy for content engagement and whether key content was seen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia view rate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent of viewers who engage with embedded multimedia (videos, images); listed as an engagement metric and also a driver of pickup when attached to releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social shares
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts shares of the release or linked content on social platforms; an engagement metric that can amplify reach and pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct republications (verbatim)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pickup metric counting outlets that publish the release text verbatim — signals syndication and broad earned distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories citing the release
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pickup metric for original news stories or articles that reference the release (not mere republication), indicating earned editorial coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes used in coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts when quotes from the release are incorporated into coverage — a qualitative sign of influence and message adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines that match release language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks whether coverage headlines mirror the release wording — indicates messaging resonance and control of narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backlinks generated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number and quality of inbound links from coverage — important for SEO and long-tail discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inbound leads attributable to release
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business metric counting leads (e.g., form fills, inquiries) that can be directly traced to the release; ties PR to pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demo requests in 7-day window
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term conversion metric to capture immediate interest; useful for campaigns with product demos or trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales pipeline impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures influence of the release on sales-qualified opportunities, revenue pipeline value, or deal progression — bottom-of-funnel business outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment inbound
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts hiring or recruitment inquiries generated by the release (relevant for employer-branding or hiring-focused announcements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarks across industries
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmarks Across Industries: Tech average: 12-15 pickups per release; Healthcare: 8-10 (regulated language); Consumer brands: 18-22; B2B SaaS: 6-8 (niche audience); Nonprofit: 14-16 (mission-driven coverage)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use industry-specific benchmark ranges to set expectations and compare performance appropriately; do not compare across industries inappropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia attached (driver)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'What Drives Higher Pickup Rates' — attaching multimedia correlates with ~1.5x higher pickup; also recommended to track multimedia separately in the quality rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-trending keyword in headline (driver)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a trend-relevant keyword in the headline correlates with ~2x lift in pickup; headline language can materially affect discoverability and pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote from C-suite (driver)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including a C-suite quote correlates with ~1.3x higher pickup — improves perceived authority and quotability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution timed Tue-Thu morning (driver)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing distribution mid-week mornings correlates with ~1.4x lift in pickup; scheduling is a controllable factor to optimize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo offered to top outlets (driver)
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargo offered to top outlets (1.8x lift)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing embargoed access to top outlets correlates with ~1.8x lift in pickup — a tactic to secure prepublication coverage from key outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common measurement mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Common Measurement Mistakes: Focusing only on impressions (vanity metric); Not tracking pipeline impact; Comparing across industries inappropriately; Missing brand mention without link; Not tracking long-tail SEO benefits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are anti-patterns to avoid when evaluating releases — focus on business outcomes and comprehensive tracking rather than vanity numbers alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting framework (funnel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting Framework: Distribution + reach (top of funnel); Engagement (middle); Pickup + sentiment (earned media); Business outcomes (bottom of funnel)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize reporting by funnel stage so stakeholders can see how top-of-funnel visibility translates into engagement, earned coverage/sentiment, and ultimately business impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tagged with UTM parameters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality requirement for measurable releases — ensure links in the release include UTM tracking to attribute traffic and conversions accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia tracked separately (quality)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure multimedia performance independently (views, plays) to understand its incremental lift and inform future creative choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment analysis enabled
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sentiment measurement on pickup/coverage to assess qualitative tone and message reception, not just volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipeline tracking integrated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate PR metrics with CRM or pipeline reporting so releases can be tied to lead generation and revenue outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-tail search visibility monitored
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track SEO and long-tail discovery over time — earned links and coverage can drive ongoing traffic beyond the immediate release window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarter-over-quarter benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare release performance over time (Q/Q) to identify trends and measure improvement rather than relying solely on single-release snapshots.
